rows.subtype: Selling with fake reviews and testimonials [Observer]
rows.description: An adult notices a page with only glowing reviews, identical wording and no negative feedback. Reading the middle-rated reviews and looking for independent sources helps find the truth.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager forwards a shocking message or story because it confirms what their group already feels. Sharing feels like loyalty, and few check the source when the message stirs anger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Repeated claims begin to feel true [Receiver]
rows.description: A person exposed again and again to the same slogan or story starts to accept it as obvious. Repetition and a clear enemy are powerful without any proof.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague or neighbour sees a rumour about a person or group spread from group to group, growing with each retelling. Harm is often done before anyone asks who first said it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wise person asks who benefits from a message, whether it aims to make them angry or afraid, and does not forward what they have not checked. Stopping a rumour is a quiet form of courage.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager sees a video or voice note of a famous person or classmate saying something shocking and believes it. Synthetic media can look and sound real, so the medium itself is no longer proof.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Why people make and share fakes [Observer]
rows.description: A teacher or friend explains that fakes are made for money, clicks, politics or cruelty, and shared by people who feel the message is true even if the details are not. Understanding motive makes it easier to doubt calmly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Deepfake used to shame or extort [Receiver]
rows.description: A young person finds fake images or videos of themselves circulating, or is threatened with them for money. It is not their fault, and saving evidence, reporting to the platform and cyber police, and telling a trusted adult are the right steps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An adult looks for the original source, searches whether trusted outlets carry the same story, and notices odd details or missing context. If it cannot be checked, it is not shared.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager who feels out of place is drawn to an intense group with rules, rituals and quick friendship. Wanting community is healthy, and the warning sign is pressure to cut off others or hide the group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
